Job Description Summary 
 The laboratory of Dr. Sungjin Ko in the Department of Regenerative Medicine and Cell Biology at the Medical University of South Carolina (MUSC) is seeking a highly motivated postdoctoral fellow for a new multi-year NIH-funded research project. 
 The postdoctoral fellow will investigate liver cancer and liver regeneration using in vitro systems, including stem cell-based models, and in vivo mouse models. Major research directions include: (a) examining the beneficial and detrimental roles of epithelial cellular plasticity in liver disease, including cell-of-origin mechanisms in intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (CCA); (b) investigating the mechanisms underlying the transition from cholestasis to CCA; and (c) identifying novel biomarkers and therapeutically actionable targets for liver cancer.

Description 
 The Aggarwal Group at UC Davis is looking for a postdoc to play a leading role in R&D toward a new tabletop radio-frequency gravitational wave detector, targeting the axion, a leading dark matter candidate. Axions can form clouds around black holes through superradiance, and those clouds emit gravitational waves. The detector concept is a Fabry-Perot Michelson interferometer with an optically trapped micro-disk in each arm cavity. It is also a promising platform for sub-SQL techniques such as sensing with squeezed light. You will work under the supervision of Prof. Aggarwal and in close collaboration with Prof. Andrew Geraci’s group at Northwestern, which is developing a companion detector, with the goal of running the two jointly. Some travel to Chicago may be needed, depending on the experiment.
